name: TSE
description: Large-scale pre-trained self-supervised learning (SSL) models have shown remarkable advancements in speech-related tasks. However, the utilization of these models in complex multi-talker scenarios, such as extracting a target speaker in a mixture, is yet to be fully evaluated. In this paper, we introduce target speech extraction (TSE) as a novel downstream task to evaluate the feature extraction capabilities of pre-trained SSL models. TSE uniquely requires both speaker identification and speech separation, distinguishing it from other tasks in the Speech processing Universal PERformance Benchmark (SUPERB) evaluation. Specifically, we propose a TSE downstream model composed of two lightweight task-oriented modules based on the same frozen SSL model. One module functions as a speaker encoder to obtain target speaker information from an enrollment speech, while the other estimates the target speaker's mask to extract its speech from the mixture. reputation: A newer SUPERB-style downstream task proposal that extends SSL speech evaluation to target speaker extraction.
notes: Task is evaluated on mixtures with enrollment speech and is sensitive to speaker overlap, mixture conditions, and downstream model design; not yet a widely standardized standalone benchmark.
